name: gerbil-scheme
desc: Opinionated dialect of Scheme designed for Systems Programming
why: A Scheme dialect built on Gambit with systems-programming leanings, offering an unusual take on Lisp for low-level work.

brief.what_it_is: Gerbil Scheme is a Scheme dialect built on the Gambit runtime and compiler, with its own macro system, module system, and standard library. It is aimed at systems programming. You write Gerbil source files or type expressions into an interactive interpreter (gxi), and the compiler (gxc) produces native code. The distribution also ships tools such as gxpkg for packages, gxtest for tests, gxprof for profiling, gxtags for tags, and gxhttpd, an HTTP server.
brief.why_it_exists: The README calls Gerbil an opinionated, some might even say tendentious, dialect of Scheme for systems programming, and says one way to think of it is as the C++ to Marc Feeley's C. The author says it began as his private Scheme and was released publicly at the prompting of friends, with a self-hosting source bootstrap on Gambit.
brief.how_it_works: The macro system is based on quote-syntax and provides a full meta-syntactic tower with a native syntax-case implementation. The module system resembles PLT/Racket modules, but per the README Gerbil modules are single-instantiation, which supports high-performance ahead-of-time compilation and compiled macros. The README says the system is entirely self-hosted, bootstrapping from source on Gambit with a precompiled macro system and compiler.

brief.install_notes: On Linux, build from source: clone the repo, run ./configure, make -j4, then sudo make install, which puts Gerbil in /opt/gerbil. Add /opt/gerbil/bin to PATH. The default configuration needs sqlite, zlib, and libcrypto/openssl; on Ubuntu, sudo apt install libssl-dev zlib1g-dev libsqlite3-dev. For the latest release, v0.18, precompiled packages exist for Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, and CentOS on the v0.18 GitHub release page. On macOS, use the brew formula from the mighty-gerbils/homebrew-gerbil tap. The README points to cons.io/guide for detailed setup. No accounts or hardware are needed.
brief.standout: Gerbil's pitch is that the macro system is the compiler: Scheme is used to build Scheme, and the README says the whole system is self-hosted. It also combines a Racket-style module system with single instantiation for ahead-of-time compilation. The README and homepage advertise actors, an integrated metaobject protocol, an FFI, and static binaries.
brief.status: Maintained, per the README. It says the project is under continuous use and development, cites a v0.18 release, and has copyright notices through 2023. I did not see a last-commit or release date, so the exact recency is unverified. The README says the core language has been stable for a while and the team is porting batteries and adding features.
brief.caveats: The README says the documentation is a work in progress. It also says the team is busy porting batteries, so parts of the library may be incomplete. Linux source builds need several system libraries. Gerbil modules are single-instantiation, which differs from Racket. The Gambit license is dual LGPLv2.1 and Apache 2.0 for the Gerbil-on-Gambit source. The homepage text I fetched was thin, so the homepage claims are high-level. The Brew formula I saw is in a separate tap, not the core. Brew gives the executable list in the user data, but I did not verify those binaries against the README.
